title: Michael Carrick unsure if Manchester United’s Matthijs de Ligt will play again this season
content:
Michael Carrick does not know if Manchester United defender Matthijs de Ligt will return from his back injury before the end of the season.

De Ligt’s last United appearance was 110 days ago – during the 2-1 win at Crystal Palace in late November, under former United head coach Ruben Amorim.

Amorim initially said De Ligt’s issue was “a small thing” and that he expected him to return for United’s trip to Wolverhampton Wanderers on December 8.

De Ligt has remained sidelined ever since, however, and is yet to return to first team training with the rest of the squad at Carrington.

Carrick has consistently stopped short of providing a specific timeline for De Ligt’s return and could offer no guarantees on Wednesday when asked if the 26-year-old will play again this season.

“It’s difficult to say, just because it’s taken that much time. I can’t give you any more on it really,” Carrick said.

“It’s one of those things with backs that sometimes you think it’s alright and then all of a sudden it’s not quite right.

“We’re just kind of being patient and working through it. We’ll just have to see. We’ll obviously give him time and try to get him back as quick as we can, but it’s really difficult to say.”

United’s head coach added: “I’m not trying to hide anything, literally at the moment we don’t know, so we’ll have to wait and see.”

Carrick admitted that De Ligt’s recovery is not progressing as quickly as hoped, having suggested in January that the Netherlands international was “getting closer” and could be back in training “hopefully in the next couple of weeks or so”.

The United head coach also said the club would need to weigh up the risks of aggravating De Ligt’s issue before making any decision on his return.

“It’s like any injury. It’s trying to get the balance right. Some are a little bit more straightforward than others. It kind of is what it is really. He’s improving, it’s not improving as quick as we all hope, but we’ll see how it goes,” he said.

Carrick refused to say whether United will need to consider surgery on De Ligt’s back if the problem persists.

“I don’t want to get into that at this stage. I think we’ll obviously try and do whatever we can to help Matta,” he added.

“I think it’ll help getting back and whatever that takes, we’re working through that now at the moment to be honest. Hopefully he’ll be back sooner rather than later and everything will be fine and we can move on.”

United travel to play Bournemouth in the Premier League on Friday evening, with Carrick’s side chasing Champions League qualification.
